focus.name: Mahogany pipe, engraved with his name
focus.description: Never smokes it in public. Taps it when he's constructing an argument. In-domain: getting a room to *listen*, getting a person to say the thing they were not going to say, getting a door to open because someone forgot he shouldn't be behind it.

meaningfulItem: Mahogany pipe engraved with his name by his uncle, the one relative he respected. Never smokes it in public; taps it when constructing an argument.
specificPlace: Battery Townsley, Marin Headlands — the abandoned WWII coastal battery he walks alone when he needs to read a speech aloud.
intentionUnderPressure: At 15 I read my first speech aloud, alone in my room, and heard the shape of a crowd I could gather. I decided then that I can see farther than the people around me and that this creates an obligation I must not decline. My parents want me finishing school. I'm not going to. School isn't teaching me anything worth staying for, and I've stopped pretending I don't already know that.
backstory:
Only child of two accomplished parents whose plans he made a career of demolishing. Discovered political speech-craft at 15 and taught himself the vocabulary of American populism. Idolizes Huey Long for the model — a man who could hold a crowd and did — not the policy. Reads speeches nightly, aloud, alone.

He is not violent. He *is* certain, in the specific way that certain 21-year-olds are, that he can see farther than the people around him and that this creates an obligation he must not decline. Alignment 'Lawful Evil' is the shape he picked because he read the description and thought *'yes, this is the honest lens.'* He would be startled to hear he was disliked. He is intermittently considering dropping out of school because he has decided school 'isn't teaching him anything worth staying for' — his parents don't know this yet.

Lives with three roommates in a shared house near Ocean Beach — Mira Sun lives eight blocks away and takes some of the same night classes at SF State. They've barely spoken outside of class; Dakota has decided she is his ally.

On the Taipei flight (Ep 1) because he had convinced himself that a small group he'd heard about *needed him* there. He was vague and self-important about it in the way people are when they don't yet have a real reason to travel abroad. The trip was fine. Nothing 'needed him.'

bonds.name: Huey Long
bonds.description: An idol. 'I know his speeches by heart. It's a damn shame he was killed. I've read every biography twice.'

bonds.name: Mira Sun
bonds.description: 'Always listens to what I tell them and takes it as gospel. Always a pleasure when people are my unquestioning followers.' — DM note: Dakota is wrong about this. Mira is watching. Keep the irony load-bearing.

dmNotes.intentionUnderPressureNote: His intent-under-pressure moment IS his self-mythology — the 15-year-old speech-reading is arrogance dressed as vocation, and Dakota does not know the difference. The character-growth arc: the FIRST time he holds a real intention (not his self-mythology) under real pressure and it *costs him something*. That's his true Phase-2 release moment. Until then his casts will keep working, but the meaning will feel hollow — which is a design feature. Do not let him access the settled-quiet release cheaply; he has to earn it by dropping the persona in a scene where the persona would have gotten him what he wanted.
dmNotes.castDomain: speech / presence — a listener's attention snaps to him and stays, a hostile crowd cools, an official reconsiders a form they were about to reject.
dmNotes.personaDropCanon: Established Ep 3 scene 03: with certain older/vulnerable NPCs (Vivian Loewe, Bea Ferro), Dakota can drop his public persona entirely — quiet, careful, gentle, patient. This is a real character choice available to the player; the persona is a defense, not the whole shape. When it drops, NPCs read it and remember.
dmNotes.controlSeekerHook: Dakota is the party's Control-seeker. Give him worthy NPCs to work; give him a mystery whose meaning he can try to own; give him a bond that quietly casts another PC as his follower (see Mira bond above) as load-bearing dramatic irony.
dmNotes.alignmentDriftWatch: If the party ever calls out his self-mythology and he *accepts* the read, he drifts toward Lawful Neutral fast. That would be earned character growth.
dmNotes.focusNotes: The pipe was engraved by his uncle, who worked wood professionally and was the one relative he respected. If the pipe breaks, an argument follows.
dmNotes.mayoralCampaign:
**Player-generated, Ep 5.** He is running for mayor of some unspecified town, presumably not San Francisco, and is unclear that February is not election season. He has begun soliciting votes — or failing that, campaign donations — from the teenagers at Ocean Beach. The poli-sci background drives it and the loud personality amplifies it. Everyone in the fiction is annoyed; the player is playing it well, which is the distinction that matters.

**The durable trait is the pattern, not the mayoralty.** It is not yet clear whether he sticks with public office or turns up next session with an entirely different grand scheme, and **either way is correct** — the character is a serial enthusiast who commits loudly and total-recalls nothing. Treat the mayoral run as *this session's instance*.

**Handling: let it run, never resolve it, never make it a real campaign.** Thirty seconds a session, not a plot. **If he arrives with a new scheme, do not have anyone mention the old one** — nobody in the fiction is keeping score, and that is funnier and truer than a callback. *(One exception: the teenagers would absolutely keep score, and would ask about the donations.)* **Ren and Maya are the right foil (T4)**: they can take the donations more seriously than he intended, or ask his platform and get a real answer. Do not let it eat table time, and do not let another PC talk him out of it.

**Where it earns its keep:** his moment-of-release arc is about dropping the persona, and a campaign is the persona in its purest public form. **If he ever quietly stops mentioning it, log that privately** — it would be a better signal than anything scripted.
dmNotes.personaEscalationLadder:
**The hinting is not landing and the player may lack the self-awareness for it yet — which is a legitimate way to play him.** Ladder, in order: **(1)** NPCs stop rewarding the persona — *fired twice in Ep 5, Ortiz cutting him off and Alaia walking away mid-pitch; he noticed neither.* **(2)** Other PCs say it to his face — cheap, try first. **(3)** An NPC names it kindly and directly; Rosa is well suited, being old enough not to care. **(4)** A private written note to the player — **already written and held** at `tmp/ep5-planning/beck-reserve-note.pdf`.

**The note does not ask him to play Dakota differently.** It offers one optional beat — Dakota noticing the thing that always worked has stopped, and being unable to work out why — and says ignoring it is a real option. **Do not deploy until rungs 2 and 3 have both been tried.** A note that reads as *play your character differently* costs more than the beat is worth.

**He already played a version of it unflagged:** handing {{pc:3}} the notebook was him reaching for a different tool because the usual one failed, and being confused about why he had to. **If that recurs, the realization is arriving on its own and the note should stay in the drawer.**

markLog.criterion: Resolved a hard moment by acting in line with alignment
markLog.note: He was the one holding the bag at the counter, and the one at the lock. When the moment needed somebody to act as though they belonged there, he did.

markLog.criterion: Took a meaningful risk for someone else
markLog.note: He put himself in front of Reggie as the bag-holder — the face Reggie was most rattled by — and took the exposure so the meeting happened.

markLog.criterion: Learned something true about The Quiet, the world, or another character
markLog.note: Absent from the table, and working. He found Bea, then the Sacramento locker, then Marsh's three ledgers, and learned the count: eight.

markLog.criterion: Took on a complication or scar that will matter later
markLog.note: Got what he wanted and paid for it. The party is no longer angry but is markedly warier, they travelled in two cars to avoid him, and he is holding a notebook the rest of them wanted to read.

markLog.criterion: Acted against your own short-term interest because the story demanded it
markLog.note: Handed Mira the notebook he had been holding since Saturday — his only leverage — after his usual approach failed in a way that visibly confused him. The hoarding finally broke, and he did not get anything for it.

inventory.vehicle: **A 12-year-old Toyota Prius**, inherited from a distant relative. One window is broken and patched with cardboard. **It is his car** — registered to him, paid for by him. **A roommate takes it anyway**, periodically, disappearing for a few days with some of everyone's stuff, forgetting to say anything, then reappearing as though nothing happened. **This is social awkwardness rather than malice: the roommate has never quite acknowledged out loud that the car belongs to somebody.** Dakota has not made an issue of it. *(Ep 3's "his roommates say he took his car and a duffel bag" is them describing his own car, correctly.)* **So it may simply not be there on any given day.**
carries: Mahogany pipe engraved with his name (focus)
Marsh's three ledgers, and the loose Argonaut paperwork from the locker, in a bag
